extracted.intended_audience: parties and practitioners participating in USPTO reexamination appeals and contested-case proceedings (appellants, respondents, patent owners, third-party requesters, counsel)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and formal requirements for filing appellant and respondent briefs, examiner answers, rebuttal briefs, oral hearings, Board decisions, rehearing, contested-case filings, motions, and related procedural papers in USPTO reexamination/appeal and contested-case proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appellant brief: required table of contents items
rubrics_metrics.description: A brief must contain the items under appropriate headings and in the order indicated in paragraphs (c)(1)(i) through (c)(1)(xi) of this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The brief must include the specific numbered subsections (i)-(xi) described below; failure to comply triggers notification and a non-extendable opportunity to amend, with dismissal consequences if not cured.

rubrics_metrics.name: Real party in interest (appellant brief)
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement identifying by name the real party in interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Placed under the specified heading in the appellant brief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Related appeals and interferences (appellant brief)
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement identifying by application, patent, appeal or interference number all other prior and pending appeals, interferences or judicial proceedings known to appellant which may be related to or affect the Board’s decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Copies of any decisions rendered by a court or the Board in any identified proceeding must be included in an appendix (see related proceedings appendix).

rubrics_metrics.name: Status of claims (appellant brief)
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement of the status of all the claims in the proceeding (e.g., rejected, allowed or confirmed, withdrawn, objected to, canceled). If the appellant is the owner, identify the rejected claims whose rejection is being appealed; if a requester, identify claims for which the examiner made a favorable determination being appealed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must clearly identify which claims are at issue and why; used by Board to determine appeal scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Status of amendments (appellant brief)
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement of the status of any amendment filed subsequent to the close of prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose whether post-prosecution amendments exist and their status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary of claimed subject matter (appellant brief)
rubrics_metrics.description: A concise explanation of the subject matter defined in each independent claim involved in the appeal, with references to the specification by column/line and to drawings by reference characters. For each independent claim (and dependent claims argued separately) identify every means-plus-function and step-plus-function limitation under 35 U.S.C. 112, sixth paragraph, and set forth corresponding structure, material, or acts in the specification with page/line and drawing references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must precisely map claim limitations to specification/drawings; means/step-plus-function limitations require explicit identification of corresponding disclosure; this is essential to Board consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issues to be reviewed on appeal (appellant brief)
rubrics_metrics.description: A concise statement of each issue presented for review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third-party requester appellants may not propose a new ground of rejection unless it was withdrawn by the examiner during prosecution and the requester has not had the opportunity to propose it previously. Each issue should be separately stated for clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Argument content and organization (appellant brief)
rubrics_metrics.description: Contentions of appellant with respect to each issue presented for review, and the basis therefor, with citations of statutes, regulations, authorities, and parts of the record relied on. Each issue must be treated under a separate heading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arguments or authorities not included in the brief (or permitted briefs under §§ 41.68 and 41.71) will be refused consideration unless good cause is shown. Mere recitation of a claim is not an argument for separate patentability. Grouped-claim arguments: claims argued as group may be decided based on a single claim selected by the Board; failure to separately argue grouped claims constitutes waiver of separate-patentability arguments. Separate headings/subheadings required for each claim or group of claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims appendix (appellant brief)
rubrics_metrics.description: An appendix containing a copy of the claims to be reviewed on appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the exact claim language as appendix material for Board review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence appendix (appellant brief)
rubrics_metrics.description: An appendix containing copies of any evidence submitted pursuant to §§ 1.130, 1.131, or 1.132 or any other evidence entered by the examiner and relied upon by appellant, with a statement setting forth where in the record that evidence was entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference to unentered evidence is not permitted; see § 41.63 for evidence after appeal. This appendix may include copies of evidence relied upon by the examiner in any ground of rejection to be reviewed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Related proceedings appendix (appellant brief)
rubrics_metrics.description: An appendix containing copies of decisions rendered by a court or the Board in any proceeding identified under related appeals/interferences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach any judicial or Board decisions relevant to related proceedings as an appendix.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of service (appellant brief)
rubrics_metrics.description: A certification that a copy of the brief has been served in its entirety on all other parties to the reexamination proceeding, including names and addresses of parties served.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certificate is required; failure risks non-consideration or dismissal consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on new or non-admitted amendments/evidence in briefs
rubrics_metrics.description: A brief shall not include any new or non-admitted amendment, or any new or non-admitted affidavit or other evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to § 1.116 for amendments/affidavits filed after final action but before or on filing appeal, and § 41.63 for evidence after filing appeal; inclusion of prohibited material can cause dismissal or non-consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Noncompliance with brief requirements (appellant)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a brief does not comply with all requirements, appellant will be notified of reasons for non-compliance and given a non-extendable time to file an amended brief; failure to timely or adequately amend will result in dismissal of the appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict procedural deadlines; amended briefs must overcome all stated reasons for non-compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent brief: scope and filing limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent(s) may once file a respondent brief within the time limit set forth in § 41.66; the brief must be signed, accompanied by fee, and is limited to issues raised in the appellant brief to which it is directed. A requester’s respondent brief may not address any brief of any other requester.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent briefs cannot expand the issues beyond those raised by appellant; signature and fee required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent brief: required content items
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent brief must contain items under appropriate headings and in order: (i) Real party in interest; (ii) Related appeals and interferences; (iii) Status of claims (accept or dispute with particularity if disputing); (iv) Status of amendments (accept or dispute with particularity); (v) Summary of claimed subject matter (accept or dispute with specification/drawing references); (vi) Issues to be reviewed (accept or dispute; may present counter statement; requester respondents may not propose new grounds); (vii) Argument accepting or disputing appellant’s contentions with citations; (viii) Evidence appendix; (ix) Related proceedings appendix; (x) Certificate of service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If disputing appellant statements, errors must be specified with particularity; each issue/argument treated under separate heading; evidence appendix must only include entered evidence; respondent brief shall not include new or non-admitted amendment/affidavit/evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Noncompliance with respondent brief requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If a respondent brief does not comply with requirements, respondent will be notified of reasons and given a non-extendable time to file an amended brief; failure to amend timely or to overcome reasons means the brief (and any amended brief) will not be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict adherence and timely cure required or brief disregarded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner’s answer: content and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: The primary examiner may furnish a written answer to appellant/respondent briefs including explanation of the invention, references relied upon, grounds of rejection, and reasons for patentability or for not adopting a proposed rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner's answer must be supplied to owner and all requesters. If examiner determines appeal non-compliant or not appealable, the examiner shall make such determination of record. Examiner’s answer may not include a new ground of rejection or a new determination not to make a proposed rejection; any new ground/determination must be in an Office action reopening prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rebuttal brief: timing and who may file
rubrics_metrics.description: Within one month of the examiner’s answer, any appellant may once file a rebuttal brief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Owner rebuttal may be directed to examiner’s answer and/or any respondent brief; requester rebuttal may be directed to examiner’s answer and/or owner respondent brief but not to another requester’s respondent brief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rebuttal brief: prohibitions on new evidence and grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Rebuttal briefs shall not include any new or non-admitted amendment, affidavit or other evidence (owner). A requester rebuttal may not propose a new ground of rejection and shall not include any new or non-admitted affidavit or other evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §1.116 and §41.63 for treatment of post-appeal evidence; strict prohibition similar to briefs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rebuttal brief: certificate of service and noncompliance
rubrics_metrics.description: The rebuttal brief must include a certification that a copy has been served in its entirety on all other parties, with names and addresses indicated. If a timely rebuttal brief does not comply with requirements, appellant will be notified and given a one-month non-extendable period to file an amended rebuttal brief; failure to timely or adequately amend will result in the rebuttal brief not being considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely cure required; one-month fixed amendment period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral hearing: when to request and how
rubrics_metrics.description: An oral hearing should be requested only when necessary or desirable for proper presentation. To request, file a separate paper captioned 'REQUEST FOR ORAL HEARING' with the fee within two months after the examiner’s answer; include certification of service and names/addresses of parties served. The time for requesting an oral hearing may not be extended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no timely request and fee, appeal will be decided on the briefs. Board may decline to hold hearing even if requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral hearing: notice, participation, and time limits
rubrics_metrics.description: If hearing requested and requirements met, a hearing date will be set and notice given; notice sets a non-extendable period for other parties to request participation. Oral argument limited to thirty minutes for each appellant or respondent requesting hearing, and twenty minutes for the primary examiner unless otherwise ordered. No party can participate unless it requested hearing and submitted the fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board determines order of arguments. Time limits are strict unless Board orders otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral hearing: evidence and argument limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: At oral hearing, each party may rely only on evidence previously entered and present argument relied upon in the briefs, except that upon a showing of good cause a party may rely on a new argument based on a recent relevant decision of the Board or a Federal Court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary examiner similarly limited; new arguments based on recent decisions require showing good cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board decisions: possible dispositions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board may affirm or reverse each decision of the examiner on issues raised on each appealed claim, or remand the reexamination proceeding to the examiner for further consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reversal of examiner’s determination not to make a requester-proposed rejection constitutes a new ground of rejection (see next items).

rubrics_metrics.name: New ground of rejection in Board decision
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Board reverses the examiner’s determination not to make a proposed rejection by a requester, the Board will set forth in its opinion a new ground of rejection; the Board may also state other grounds not raised in the appeal as a new ground of rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any decision including a new ground of rejection is not final for judicial review. When a new ground is made, owner within one month must either (1) reopen prosecution (file response/amendment or new evidence) or (2) request rehearing addressing the new ground with particularity. Time periods for following actions are specified and some are non-extendable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Owner options after Board new ground of rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Within one month of the decision, owner must either (1) reopen prosecution by filing an amendment or new evidence relating to the claims so rejected, or (2) request rehearing by the Board addressing the new ground and stating with particularity points believed misapprehended or overlooked and all other grounds for rehearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reopen prosecution response must be an amendment or new evidence (or both) directed to the new ground; requesting rehearing must be timely and specific.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments and replies after owner response to new ground
rubrics_metrics.description: Where owner reopens prosecution, any requester may within one month of service of owner’s response once file comments limited to issues raised by the Board’s opinion and owner’s response. Those who had not previously filed appeals and seek to file comments/replies are subject to appeal and brief fees which must accompany the comments or reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Following comments/replies the proceeding is remanded to the examiner; the Board’s statement is binding unless overcome by amendment/new evidence not previously of record. Time limits are strict and some are non-extendable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rehearing: timing and required content
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties may file a request for rehearing within one month of specified decisions (original decision, §41.77(b) decision, expiration of owner time under §41.77(b)(2), or new decision under §41.77(f)). The request must state with particularity the points believed to have been misapprehended or overlooked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arguments not raised in briefs and evidence not previously relied upon are not permitted in rehearing requests except as allowed by good cause or to respond to a new ground of rejection. Comments in opposition may be filed within one month and limited to issues raised in the rehearing request. Times to request rehearing/comments may not be extended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contested-case general conduct and default rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board may determine proper conduct for situations not specifically covered and may enter non-final orders; an administrative patent judge may waive/suspend application of any rule in the subpart subject to conditions; times set in the subpart are defaults and an order’s time controls over a rule when in conflict. Action due on a non-business day may be done next business day unless Board states otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board has procedural flexibility in contested cases; parties must follow orders and default time rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing format requirements (papers and exhibits)
rubrics_metrics.description: Paper must be durable and white; choose EITHER A4 or 8.5×11-inch paper for a proceeding (can't switch sizes); only one side used. Markings in black ink or equivalent; printing quality equivalent to laser; proportional font must be 12-point or larger; monospaced font no more than 4 characters/cm (10 per inch); case names underlined or italicized. Double spacing except headings, TOC, tables of authorities, indices, signature blocks, certificates of service; block quotations may be single-spaced and indented. Margins at least 2.5 cm (1 inch) all sides.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exhibits that require larger size permitted. Non-complying formatting can be grounds for non-consideration or demand to amend.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover sheet and physical paper requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Cover sheet must include caption specified by Board, header indicating party and contact information, and a title indicating sequence and subject of paper (e.g., 'JONES MOTION 2, For benefit of an earlier application'). If Board specifies a cover sheet color other than white, use that color. Papers must have two 0.5 cm holes centered horizontally 1 cm from top and 7 cm apart.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow cover sheet format and hole placement exactly; combining papers or incorporating arguments by reference is prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: No incorporation by reference or combined papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Arguments must not be incorporated by reference from one paper into another; combined motions, oppositions, replies, or other combined papers are not permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each motion must be a separate paper and self-contained regarding arguments and required showings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Working copy requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Every paper filed must be accompanied by a working copy marked 'APJ Copy'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide working copy to assist the administrative patent judge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing by mail and other modes of filing
rubrics_metrics.description: Express Mail filings using USPS EXPRESS MAIL service deemed filed as of 'date-in' on the EXPRESS MAIL mailing label; otherwise mail filed as of stamped date of receipt at the Board. Board may authorize other modes (electronic, hand filing) and set conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow specified filing modes and preserve evidence of filing date when using Express Mail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service method and certificate of service requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers filed with the Board must be served simultaneously on all opposing parties unless Board directs otherwise. If party is represented, service must be on counsel. Service must be by EXPRESS MAIL or means at least as fast and reliable; electronic service not permitted without Board authorization. Date of service does not count in computing response time. Papers (other than exhibits) must include a certificate of service as a separate page stating date/manner of service, name/address of every person served, and for grouped exhibits the name/number of each exhibit; certificates by non-practitioners must be in form of an affidavit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict service requirements; failure to properly serve or include required certificate may result in non-consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead counsel identification and contact information
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 14 days of initiation of each contested case, each party must file a notice identifying its counsel (or if none, the party) and provide contact information including mailing address, courier delivery address (if needed), telephone number, facsimile number, and electronic mail address. If counsel not of record in involved application/patent, a power of attorney for that counsel must be filed with the notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties must promptly notify Board of any contact information changes. Board may require appointment of lead counsel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to and copies of Office records
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for access or copies of Office records directly related to a contested case must be filed with the Board and must precisely identify the records; copies require appropriate fee. Access/ copies ordinarily authorized for the application file for an involved patent, an involved application, and applications for which a party is accorded benefit under subpart E. If a party does not receive a complete copy within 21 days of authorization, notify the Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be precise in requests and pay fees; follow notification requirements for missing/incomplete copies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing claim information: clean and annotated copies
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 14 days of initiation, each party must file a clean copy of its involved claims and, if a biotechnology material sequence is a limitation, a clean copy of the sequence. Within 28 days of initiation, each party must file annotated copies: (1) for claims with limitations illustrated in a drawing or sequence, indicate in bold-face between braces where each limitation is shown; (2) for means-plus-function or step-plus-function limitations under 35 U.S.C. 112(6), indicate in bold-face between braces the specific portions of the specification that describe corresponding structure, material, or acts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accurate annotation linking claim limitations to the disclosure is mandatory; motions to add/amend claims must include clean copy, claim chart showing written-description locations, and annotated claims when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of basis for relief and its effect
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board may require a party to provide a notice stating the relief requested and the basis for entitlement. The Board may keep the notice confidential for a limited time. If required, a party will be limited to filing substantive motions consistent with the notice; ambiguities construed against the party. A notice is not evidence except as an admission by an opposing party. Party may move to correct its notice; corrections after the time set will be entered only if entry would serve the interests of justice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice defines permissible substantive motions; be precise and timely; correct promptly if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of material facts and claim chart requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers requiring factual statements must include a statement of material facts with each material fact separately stated as a numbered sentence with specific citations to record portions that support the fact. The Board may require that the statement be a separate paper. Claim charts must be used in support of any paper requiring comparison of a claim to something else (another claim, prior art, or a specification) and must accompany the paper as an appendix; claim charts are not a substitute for argument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any material fact not specifically denied is considered admitted in oppositions/replies. Ensure claim charts and numbered factual statements accompany motions and are well-cited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motions: types and burden of proof
rubrics_metrics.description: Types: substantive motions (e.g., to redefine scope of contested case, change benefit accorded, judgment in contested case), responsive motions (e.g., to amend/add a claim, change inventorship), and miscellaneous motions. The party filing the motion has the burden of proof to establish entitlement to requested relief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File motions consistent with any required notice of relief; burden rests on movant; choose correct motion type and provide supporting material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motions: required content, showings, and compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Each motion must be filed as a separate paper and include (i) a statement of the precise relief requested, (ii) a statement of material facts, and (iii) a full statement of the reasons for the relief requested, including detailed explanation of the significance of the evidence and governing law, rules, and precedent. Where a rule in part 1 ordinarily governs the relief sought, the motion must make any showings required under that rule in addition to required showings in this part. The Board may order additional showings or explanations as a condition for filing a motion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Motions must be comprehensive and self-contained; failure to include required showings may lead to denial or rejection of the motion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oppositions and replies: compliance and disputed facts
rubrics_metrics.description: Oppositions and replies must comply with content requirements for motions and must include a statement identifying material facts in dispute; any material fact not specifically denied shall be considered admitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondents must explicitly deny material facts they dispute and provide citations; otherwise facts are deemed admitted, adversely affecting positions.
